I will still farm the 3.1 mu the way I know works here: one wheat crop, then one maize crop on the same land. I do not start from empty. I look at what I did last year, what the neighbors around Quzhou County are doing, and what gives a steady harvest without spending money foolishly. My land is small, so every bag I buy matters, but I also do not want to save a little on fertilizer and then lose a lot in yield. With well irrigation, I will keep wheat fed a bit heavier because wheat on our side needs water and fertilizer together to make heads well. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people do now, because I have seen it yield better than old seed if fertilizer and water keep up. I will keep phosphorus and potassium in the base fertilizer, then put most nitrogen in split doses so the crop does not go hungry at the key stage. Wheat I will irrigate 3 times if the year is normal, maize 2 times. My land is only 3.1 mu and some family members work outside, so I will choose methods that save labor and do not miss the season, especially for summer maize after wheat harvest.
